title: 30 Apartment Decorating Ideas for Every Room and Budget
h1: 30 Apartment Decorating Ideas for Every Room (With Budget Tags)
description: 30 apartment decorating ideas sorted by room, each tagged by budget: renter-friendly ways to add warmth, style and storage without losing your deposit.
excerpt: Thirty renter-friendly apartment decorating ideas grouped by room, each tagged by budget, plus a step-by-step plan for decorating an apartment from scratch.
image_alt: Apartment decorating ideas in a cozy living room with a gray sofa, rust and mustard pillows, abstract art, a round mirror and a jute rug
key_takeaways: Warm 2700K bulbs and three lamps per room are the cheapest, highest-impact upgrade.
Hang curtains 4 to 6 inches below the ceiling and size rugs so front furniture legs sit on them.
One large piece of art looks more expensive than many small frames.
Choose a three-to-five-color palette before you buy anything.
Nearly every idea is renter-friendly; get written permission before painting or drilling.

faq.q: How do I decorate my apartment with no money?
faq.a: Start with free changes: declutter every surface, rearrange furniture so the sofa floats off the wall, group the objects you already own in odd numbers, and move lamps so light comes from several heights. Shop your own home for art, plants and textiles, and swap items between rooms. Clipping greenery from outside or framing free prints also costs almost nothing.

faq.q: How can I make my apartment look cute?
faq.a: Layer soft textures like a knit throw and textured pillows, add warm fairy lights or small lamps, bring in plants, and display a few personal objects in matching frames. A cohesive palette with one or two soft accent colors keeps cute from tipping into cluttered. Edit regularly so each piece has space to stand out.

faq.q: What should I buy first when decorating an apartment?
faq.a: Buy a comfortable mattress and sofa first, since you use them daily, then warm bulbs and lamps, full-length curtains and a correctly sized rug. Those basics set the look of every room. Art, pillows, plants and accessories come last because they are cheap to change and easier to choose once the larger pieces are in place.

faq.q: How do you decorate a rental apartment without damaging walls?
faq.a: Use removable adhesive hooks and strips, picture ledges, leaned floor mirrors and art, tension rods for curtains and shower curtains, and plug-in sconces with cord covers. Peel-and-stick backsplash and removable wallpaper work in many rentals, but test a small patch first. Always check your lease before making changes.

faq.q: How much does it cost to decorate an apartment?
faq.a: It varies widely. A refresh using bulbs, lamps, curtains, a rug and art typically runs a few hundred to about $1,500 for a one-bedroom. Furnishing from scratch with new mid-range pieces often costs several thousand dollars or more. Buying secondhand furniture and spending most on the sofa and mattress stretches any budget.
